packages.angle: A cancelled-manga underdog just became one of the biggest shonen shows on streaming this summer
packages.hook_onscreen_text: Black Torch's manga got cancelled after just 19 chapters.
hook_candidates: Black Torch's manga got cancelled after just 19 chapters.
Everyone wrote off Black Torch as a failed manga. Nobody expected the anime to outperform half the summer lineup.
packages.hook_line: Black Torch's manga got cancelled after just 19 chapters.
packages.opening_sentence: Black Torch's manga got cancelled after just 19 chapters.
packages.vo: Black Torch's manga got cancelled after just 19 chapters. Its anime adaptation just became one of the biggest shows on streaming. Ichika, Jiro, and Rago meet in the very first episode, and by episode seven, Rago's full power finally gets its moment. Episode two brings a real confrontation between Jiro and his grandfather, the kind of family stakes the story builds around. This is 100studio's fourth production, and the squad's action sequences move with real polish. Would you have picked up a manga if you knew going in that it would get cancelled at just 19 chapters? Leave your take.
vo_fact_beats: Black Torch's source manga by Tsuyoshi Takaki ran in Jump Square from December 2016 to March 2018 -- only 19 chapters across 5 volumes -- and was widely treated as a cancelled, underperforming series before the anime was greenlit.

The anime premiered July 4, 2026 on Tokyo MX and affiliates, produced by 100studio (only their 4th production), directed by Kei Umabiki, with series composition by Gigaemon Ichikawa and character design by Gô Suzuki; it is currently airing Saturdays 22:00 JST.

Premise: Jiro Azuma, descended from a shinobi clan and able to talk to animals, rescues an injured black cat that turns out to be Rago, an immortal mononoke called the Black Star of Doom; Jiro is mortally wounded defending Rago, who fuses with him to save his life and grant him powers, and he's recruited into the Bureau of Espionage's 'Black Torch' squad to fight rogue mononoke.

As of a MovieWeb piece dated August 11, 2026, Black Torch is described as officially one of the biggest shows on streaming for the season -- a genuine reversal for source material that had been considered a failed, cancelled manga.
The show is still airing as of this post date; per Smart Calendars' summer 2026 schedule, Episode 8 airs August 22, 2026, one day after this post.

packages.angle: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and in production, but Crunchyroll is holding it back for one specific reason
packages.hook_onscreen_text: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and already in production.
hook_candidates: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and already in production.
D&C Media confirmed Solo Leveling Season 3 months ago. So why is Crunchyroll still refusing to give it a release date?
packages.hook_line: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and already in production.
packages.opening_sentence: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and already in production.
packages.vo: Solo Leveling Season 3 is confirmed and already in production. But Crunchyroll is holding it back, and the evidence points to one specific reason: a bridge film has to come first. Sung Jinwoo's true power showed up in episode nineteen, then got tested against the Ant King, then tested again when Beru first shadow-arises to fight at his side. That escalation needs a bridge before Season 3 can properly pay it off. Sequencing the film first keeps that pipeline continuous instead of jumping straight to the next arc. Would you rather get the bridge movie first, or skip straight to Season 3? Leave your take.
vo_fact_beats: D&C Media, the webtoon's original publisher and a major investor in the anime, officially confirmed Season 3 is in production in its June 9, 2026 investor report, with a target release window of 2027-2028; A-1 Pictures and Aniplex remain the production studios.

A bridge project, the film 'Solo Leveling: Beyond the System,' was announced July 3, 2026 at Anime Expo during the Crunchyroll Showcase; it picks up directly after Season 2 and targets a 2027 release, explicitly positioned as a bridge INTO Season 3, not a replacement for it.

Per Game Rant (Aug 14, 2026), Crunchyroll briefly labeled the bridge film 'Season 3' in early marketing before removing that label after fan confusion, clarifying the film and the true TV Season 3 are separate projects.

Per The Direct (Aug 18, 2026) -- the most recent dated development -- Crunchyroll will not release Solo Leveling Season 3 until after the Beyond the System film comes out first, reconfirming the 2027-2028 D&C Media window as still current.
Crunchyroll CEO Rahul Purini confirmed active development in a May 22, 2026 interview with Radio Times, without giving a release date.
Expected content scope for Season 3, per multiple outlets, is roughly manga chapters 111-140/150, covering the Ahjin Guild's formation and the Architect mystery inside the Double Dungeon.
